question: A nurse caring for a 55-year-old man on the ward after an operation notes a dry mouth, a fast pulse and dark urine. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Encourage fluids and check the fluid balance chart
option_2: Restrict fluids until the doctor reviews him
option_3: Give a diuretic so that he passes more urine
option_4: Record the findings and wait for the ward round
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Encourage fluids and check the fluid balance chart

Clinical Rationale: A dry mouth, a fast pulse and dark urine point to NOT enough fluid, so fluids are encouraged and the chart is checked.

Key Clue: a dry mouth with a fast pulse and dark urine

Priority Principle: Fluid deficit

Why Not Others: (b) Restricting fluid makes the deficit worse; (c) A diuretic would remove more fluid; (d) Waiting lets the fluid deficit grow.

PGI Exam Trap: Fluids are restricted until the doctor reviews him.

5-Second Recall: Encourage fluids and check the fluid balance.

PNC Exam Pearl: Dry mouth and dark urine mean more fluid.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 45-year-old woman on the ward with a new ileostomy has a very high output of watery stool. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Wait and see if the output settles by night
option_2: Restrict all fluids to dry up the stoma
option_3: Give a strong laxative to clear the bowel
option_4: Give oral fluids with salt and tell the doctor
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Give oral fluids with salt and tell the doctor

Clinical Rationale: A very high ileostomy output loses water and salts, so oral fluids with salt are given and the doctor is told.

Key Clue: a new ileostomy with a very high output

Priority Principle: High ileostomy output

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting lets the man lose more salts; (b) Restricting fluids makes the loss worse; (c) A laxative would raise the output further.

PGI Exam Trap: A strong laxative is given to clear the bowel.

5-Second Recall: Give oral fluids with salt and tell the doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: A wet stoma loses water and salt.

question: A nurse on the ward must set the order of steps to collect a blood culture from a 50-year-old man with a fever. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST steps?
option_1: Take the blood after the antibiotics are given
option_2: Put the needle down FIRST and then clean the skin
option_3: Clean the skin, take the blood, then put it into the bottle
option_4: Send a dry syringe to the lab without a bottle
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Clean the skin, take the blood, then put it into the bottle

Clinical Rationale: The skin is cleaned, the blood is taken, and it goes straight into the bottle so that the sample stays clean.

Key Clue: the steps for a blood culture

Priority Principle: Blood culture order

Why Not Others: (a) Antibiotics are given after the culture; (b) The skin is cleaned before the needle is used; (d) The blood goes into a culture bottle.

PGI Exam Trap: The needle is put down before the skin is cleaned.

5-Second Recall: Clean the skin, take the blood, bottle it.

PNC Exam Pearl: Clean, take, bottle.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked why a wound swab is taken before antibiotics are started. Which statement is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The swab is taken later so that it is cleaner
option_2: The antibiotics may stop the germs from growing in the lab
option_3: Antibiotics help the germs to grow in the bottle
option_4: The swab is taken after the wound has healed
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The antibiotics may stop the germs from growing in the lab

Clinical Rationale: Antibiotics can stop the germs growing in the lab, so the swab is taken before they are started.

Key Clue: why a swab is taken before antibiotics

Priority Principle: Culture before antibiotics

Why Not Others: (a) A later swab is not the reason to wait; (c) Antibiotics do not help the germs grow; (d) A healed wound needs no swab taken.

PGI Exam Trap: The swab is taken after the antibiotics are started.

5-Second Recall: Take the swab before the antibiotics.

PNC Exam Pearl: Swab first, drug next.

question: A community nurse visits a family whose child has NOT had the measles vaccine. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Tell the family that they must pay a fine
option_2: Explain the benefits and arrange the missed vaccine
option_3: Give the vaccine without any explanation
option_4: Write the family off as non-compliant
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Explain the benefits and arrange the missed vaccine

Clinical Rationale: The nurse explains the benefits in plain words and arranges the missed vaccine so the child is protected.

Key Clue: a child who has missed the measles vaccine

Priority Principle: Missed immunisation

Why Not Others: (a) A fine does not win the family over; (c) Consent and explanation come before the dose; (d) The family is helped, not written off.

PGI Exam Trap: The family is written off as non-compliant.

5-Second Recall: Explain the benefits and arrange the missed vaccine.

PNC Exam Pearl: Explain first, then protect the child.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which finding is the MOST likely to show that a wound is infected rather than healing.
option_1: A small amount of fresh blood at the edge
option_2: A thin clear fluid with no smell
option_3: Thick yellow discharge with a bad smell
option_4: A clean dry line with light scabbing
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Thick yellow discharge with a bad smell

Clinical Rationale: Thick bad-smelling yellow discharge points to infection, while clear fluid or a dry line suggests normal healing.

Key Clue: a wound with thick yellow discharge

Priority Principle: Wound infection

Why Not Others: (a) A little fresh blood at the edge is common; (b) A thin clear fluid suggests normal healing; (d) A clean dry line suggests healing.

PGI Exam Trap: A thin clear fluid with no smell is called infection.

5-Second Recall: Thick bad-smelling discharge shows infection.

PNC Exam Pearl: Smell and pus mean infection.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward is asked about sharing her medical details with her family. Which statement is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Details are shared with anyone who visits the ward
option_2: Details are shared freely with any close relative
option_3: Details are shared with the family as a rule
option_4: Details are shared after the woman gives permission
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Details are shared after the woman gives permission

Clinical Rationale: Patient details stay private and are shared with the family once the woman gives her own permission.

Key Clue: sharing a woman's medical details with her family

Priority Principle: Confidentiality

Why Not Others: (a) Visitors are not told anything at all; (b) A close relative still needs her permission; (c) The family does not get details as a rule.

PGI Exam Trap: Details are shared with the family as a rule.

5-Second Recall: Share details only after the woman agrees.

PNC Exam Pearl: Her details, her choice.

question: A community nurse on a survey must set the order of steps to check the blood pressure of an elderly resident. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST steps?
option_1: Let him rest, put the cuff on the arm, then take a reading
option_2: Take the reading FIRST and then let him rest
option_3: Put the cuff on the leg and take the reading
option_4: Ask him to walk briskly and then take it at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Let him rest, put the cuff on the arm, then take a reading

Clinical Rationale: The resident rests FIRST, the cuff is placed on the arm, and then the reading is taken for a true result.

Key Clue: the steps for a correct blood pressure reading

Priority Principle: Blood pressure order

Why Not Others: (b) The reading comes after the rest; (c) The cuff goes on the arm, not the leg; (d) Walking first gives a false high reading.

PGI Exam Trap: The reading is taken FIRST and then he rests.

5-Second Recall: Rest, cuff on the arm, then read.

PNC Exam Pearl: Rest first, read last.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A community nurse visits a family and must set the order of steps to check a child at home. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST steps?
option_1: Greet the family, look at the child, then give advice
option_2: Give advice FIRST, then greet and look
option_3: Look at the child, give advice, then greet
option_4: Greet the family, give advice, then look at the child
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Greet the family, look at the child, then give advice

Clinical Rationale: The nurse greets the family, looks at the child next, and gives advice after seeing how the child is.

Key Clue: the steps for a home visit

Priority Principle: Home visit order

Why Not Others: (b) Advice comes after the greeting and look; (c) The greeting comes before the look; (d) The child is looked at before advice.

PGI Exam Trap: The advice is given before the child is looked at.

5-Second Recall: Greet, look, then advise.

PNC Exam Pearl: Greet, see, then say.

question: A nurse manager on the ward must set the order of steps to manage a staffing shortage over a 12-hour shift. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST steps?
option_1: Wait for the shortage to pass on its own
option_2: Move staff FIRST and then check the numbers
option_3: Call for help FIRST and then check the numbers
option_4: Check the ward numbers, call for help, then move staff
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Check the ward numbers, call for help, then move staff

Clinical Rationale: The ward numbers are checked, help is called, and staff are moved only after that.

Key Clue: the steps to manage a staffing shortage

Priority Principle: Staffing order

Why Not Others: (a) A shortage is managed, not waited out; (b) Staff are not moved before the numbers; (c) The numbers are checked before help is called.

PGI Exam Trap: Staff are moved before the ward numbers are checked.

5-Second Recall: Check the numbers, call for help, then move staff.

PNC Exam Pearl: Count first, call next.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward after a stroke is asked which position is the MOST appropriate to keep his airway safe.
option_1: Sitting fully upright at 90 degrees
option_2: Lying flat on his back with no pillow
option_3: Lying on his side with the head slightly raised
option_4: Lying face down on the stomach
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Lying on his side with the head slightly raised

Clinical Rationale: Lying on the side with the head slightly raised stops the tongue falling back and keeps the airway clear.

Key Clue: the safe position for a man after a stroke

Priority Principle: Airway position

Why Not Others: (a) Sitting fully upright does not protect the airway; (b) Lying flat lets the tongue fall back; (d) Lying face down blocks the breathing.

PGI Exam Trap: The man is laid flat on his back to protect the airway.

5-Second Recall: A sideways position with the head raised keeps the airway open.

PNC Exam Pearl: On the side, head up a little.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who takes the drug metformin is sent for a scan with contrast dye. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Give the metformin with the dye as usual
option_2: Hold the metformin and tell the doctor before the scan
option_3: Double the metformin dose after the scan
option_4: Stop the drug and give no reason to the doctor
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Hold the metformin and tell the doctor before the scan

Clinical Rationale: Contrast dye with metformin can harm the kidneys, so the drug is held and the doctor told before the scan.

Key Clue: metformin with a contrast scan

Priority Principle: Metformin and contrast

Why Not Others: (a) The dye with metformin can harm the kidneys; (c) The dose is not doubled after the scan; (d) The doctor is told why the drug is held.

PGI Exam Trap: The metformin is given with the dye as usual.

5-Second Recall: Hold the metformin and tell the doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: Contrast plus metformin hurt the kidneys.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward notes that his urine output has fallen to 20 ml in the last hour. Which is the MOST likely cause for the nurse to consider?
option_1: A rise in the blood flow to the kidneys
option_2: A fall in the blood flow to the kidneys
option_3: A high fluid intake within the hour
option_4: A large amount of fluid drunk at home
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) A fall in the blood flow to the kidneys

Clinical Rationale: A urine output of only 20 ml in an hour points to less blood reaching the kidneys, so the cause is looked for.

Key Clue: a urine output of 20 ml in an hour

Priority Principle: Low urine output

Why Not Others: (a) More blood flow would raise the output; (c) A high fluid intake would raise it; (d) Drinking a lot would raise the output.

PGI Exam Trap: The low output is blamed on a high fluid intake.

5-Second Recall: A urine output of 20 ml an hour points to poor kidney flow.

PNC Exam Pearl: 20 ml an hour is too little.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward notes that her contractions have been strong for 3 hours and are now one on top of another. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Call the doctor and stop the oxytocin drug
option_2: Give more oxytocin to speed the labour
option_3: Leave her alone to rest between contractions
option_4: Tell her that this pattern is quite normal
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Call the doctor and stop the oxytocin drug

Clinical Rationale: Contractions one on top of another point to too much oxytocin, so the drug is stopped and the doctor called at once.

Key Clue: contractions one on top of another after 3 hours

Priority Principle: Excess oxytocin

Why Not Others: (b) More oxytocin would make it worse; (c) There is no rest, so she is not left alone; (d) This pattern is not normal and needs care.

PGI Exam Trap: More oxytocin is given to speed up the labour.

5-Second Recall: Call the doctor and stop the oxytocin.

PNC Exam Pearl: Too many contractions mean too much drug.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about giving morphine for pain is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: Stop watching the man once the pain eases
option_2: Give a double dose whenever the pain is bad
option_3: Give it with no regard to the breathing rate
option_4: Watch for slow breathing and a falling blood pressure
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Watch for slow breathing and a falling blood pressure

Clinical Rationale: Morphine can slow the breathing and drop the blood pressure, so both are watched after every dose.

Key Clue: what to watch after giving morphine

Priority Principle: Opioid safety

Why Not Others: (a) Watching continues after the pain eases; (b) The dose is not doubled for worse pain; (c) The breathing rate is always checked.

PGI Exam Trap: A double dose is given whenever the pain is bad.

5-Second Recall: Watch for slow breathing and a low blood pressure.

PNC Exam Pearl: Morphine slows the breath.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a 4-year-old child on the ward is asked which finding shows that the child is short of fluid.
option_1: A strong cry with plenty of tears
option_2: A wet nappy every hour with pink skin
option_3: A sunken soft spot with few wet nappies
option_4: A good appetite with regular stools
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) A sunken soft spot with few wet nappies

Clinical Rationale: A sunken soft spot with few wet nappies points to NOT enough fluid in a young child.

Key Clue: the signs of NOT enough fluid in a young child

Priority Principle: Dehydration in a child

Why Not Others: (a) A strong cry with tears is reassuring; (b) A wet nappy every hour is a good sign; (d) A good appetite is not a fluid deficit.

PGI Exam Trap: A wet nappy every hour shows the child is short of fluid.

5-Second Recall: A sunken soft spot and few wet nappies show fluid loss.

PNC Exam Pearl: Few wet nappies means dry.

question: A nurse caring for a 30-year-old man on the ward who hears voices tells the nurse that he cannot sleep. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ignore it and finish the ward round
option_2: Tell him that the voices are NOT real
option_3: Give a sleeping tablet and leave him
option_4: Ask him what the voices are saying to him
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Ask him what the voices are saying to him

Clinical Rationale: The nurse asks what the voices are saying so that any risk of harm is understood before anything else.

Key Clue: a man who hears voices and cannot sleep

Priority Principle: Command hallucinations

Why Not Others: (a) The complaint is not ignored; (b) Arguing about the voices does not help; (c) A tablet alone hides the risk.

PGI Exam Trap: A sleeping tablet is given and the voices are set aside.

5-Second Recall: Ask him what the voices are saying.

PNC Exam Pearl: What the voices say is the risk.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward with severe diarrhoea notes that he feels weak and his heart is racing. Which finding is the MOST likely for the nurse to expect?
option_1: A low blood potassium level with weakness
option_2: A high blood potassium level with weakness
option_3: A high blood calcium level with weakness
option_4: A high blood sugar level with weakness
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) A low blood potassium level with weakness

Clinical Rationale: Severe diarrhoea loses potassium from the body, so a low blood potassium level is expected with weakness and a racing heart.

Key Clue: severe diarrhoea with weakness and a racing heart

Priority Principle: Potassium loss

Why Not Others: (b) Diarrhoea lowers, not raises, potassium; (c) Calcium is not the level lost here; (d) Blood sugar is not the cause of this.

PGI Exam Trap: A high blood potassium level is expected with diarrhoea.

5-Second Recall: Severe diarrhoea gives a low blood potassium.

PNC Exam Pearl: Diarrhoea drains potassium.

Reference Table: Normal serum electrolyte ranges - Sodium (Na+): 135-145 mEq/L; Potassium (K+): 3.5-5.0 mEq/L; Chloride (Cl-): 98-106 mEq/L; Calcium (total): 8.5-10.5 mg/dL; Magnesium (Mg2+): 1.5-2.5 mEq/L; Phosphate: 3.0-4.5 mg/dL.

question: A nurse caring for a 70-year-old man on the ward before an operation is asked about stopping smoking. Which action is the BEST for the nurse to take?
option_1: Tell him that smoking cannot be stopped now
option_2: Explain the benefits of stopping before the operation
option_3: Ignore the habit as it is his own choice
option_4: Give him extra cigarettes to keep him calm
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Explain the benefits of stopping before the operation

Clinical Rationale: Stopping smoking even a few weeks before an operation lowers the risk of chest and wound problems.

Key Clue: a man before an operation who smokes

Priority Principle: Preoperative smoking

Why Not Others: (a) Stopping now does help before surgery; (c) The nurse guides him, not ignores it; (d) Extra cigarettes raise the risk.

PGI Exam Trap: The habit is ignored as his own choice.

5-Second Recall: Explain the benefits of stopping before surgery.

PNC Exam Pearl: Stop the smoke, lower the risk.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has a chest drain is asked which finding is the MOST important to report.
option_1: A small amount of clear fluid in the bottle
option_2: Gentle swinging of the fluid with each breath
option_3: Sudden bubbling with a lot of pain
option_4: A calm man with a steady pulse
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Sudden bubbling with a lot of pain

Clinical Rationale: Sudden bubbling with a lot of pain points to a leak or a blocked drain, so it is reported at once.

Key Clue: a chest drain with sudden bubbling and pain

Priority Principle: Chest drain leak

Why Not Others: (a) A little clear fluid is expected; (b) Gentle swinging with each breath is normal; (d) A calm man with a steady pulse is not a warning.

PGI Exam Trap: Gentle swinging of the fluid is reported as a danger.

5-Second Recall: Sudden bubbling with a lot of pain is reported.

PNC Exam Pearl: Bubbling plus pain means a leak.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward who takes levothyroxine is also started on iron tablets. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Stop the levothyroxine without telling anyone
option_2: Give both drugs together each morning
option_3: Separate the two drugs by some hours
option_4: Give a double dose of iron each day
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Separate the two drugs by some hours

Clinical Rationale: Iron blocks the uptake of levothyroxine, so the two drugs are taken some hours apart.

Key Clue: levothyroxine started with iron tablets

Priority Principle: Drug absorption

Why Not Others: (a) The thyroid drug is not stopped in secret; (b) Together the iron blocks the thyroid drug; (d) The iron dose is not doubled.

PGI Exam Trap: Both drugs are given together each morning.

5-Second Recall: Separate the two drugs by a few hours.

PNC Exam Pearl: Iron in the way, thyroid held up.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is about to give an injection into the buttock. Which action is the BEST to avoid harm?
option_1: Give the drug without checking the order
option_2: Give it into the middle of the buttock
option_3: Use a long needle and push it fully in
option_4: Check the site and use the upper outer part
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Check the site and use the upper outer part

Clinical Rationale: An injection into the upper outer part of the buttock avoids the nerve that runs through the middle.

Key Clue: the safe site for an injection into the buttock

Priority Principle: Injection site

Why Not Others: (a) The order is checked before any drug; (b) The middle of the buttock holds a large nerve; (c) A long needle pushed fully is unsafe.

PGI Exam Trap: The injection is put into the middle of the buttock.

5-Second Recall: Use the upper outer part of the buttock.

PNC Exam Pearl: Upper outer, away from the nerve.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has been vomiting is asked which drink is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to give him.
option_1: An oral rehydration solution in small sips
option_2: A large glass of strong tea
option_3: A sweet fizzy drink taken quickly
option_4: Plain cold water in one go
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) An oral rehydration solution in small sips

Clinical Rationale: Small sips of an oral rehydration solution replace both the water and the salts lost in vomiting.

Key Clue: what to give a man after vomiting

Priority Principle: Oral rehydration

Why Not Others: (b) Strong tea does not replace the salts; (c) A fizzy drink is too sugary and quick; (d) Water in one go is not the best choice.

PGI Exam Trap: A large glass of strong tea is given after vomiting.

5-Second Recall: Give an oral rehydration solution in small sips.

PNC Exam Pearl: Sip water and salts after vomiting.

question: A nurse caring for a 65-year-old man on the ward who had a heart attack reports a new loud murmur and a cold sweaty skin. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Note it and report it on the next round
option_2: Call the doctor at once and stay with him
option_3: Give him a drink and let him rest
option_4: Ask the family to keep him company
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Call the doctor at once and stay with him

Clinical Rationale: A new loud murmur with a cold sweaty skin after a heart attack points to a rupture, so the doctor is called at once.

Key Clue: a new loud murmur after a heart attack

Priority Principle: Heart rupture

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting risks a sudden collapse; (c) A drink and rest do not treat this; (d) The family cannot watch this danger.

PGI Exam Trap: The murmur is noted and reported on the next round.

5-Second Recall: Call the doctor at once and stay with him.

PNC Exam Pearl: New murmur after a heart attack is an emergency.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward is asked which action is the BEST to stop the spread of infection between patients.
option_1: Share a stethoscope without cleaning it
option_2: Clean the hands once at the end of the shift
option_3: Wear the same gloves for many patients
option_4: Clean the hands before and after each patient
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Clean the hands before and after each patient

Clinical Rationale: Cleaning the hands before and after every patient is the main way to stop germs passing between people.

Key Clue: how to stop infection passing between patients

Priority Principle: Hand hygiene

Why Not Others: (a) Shared tools are cleaned between patients; (b) Once at the end of a shift is not enough; (c) Gloves are changed for each patient.

PGI Exam Trap: The hands are cleaned only at the end of the shift.

5-Second Recall: Clean the hands before and after each patient.

PNC Exam Pearl: Clean hands, stop the germs.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward in a side room with a chest infection is asked about the shut door. Which statement is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It stops the man from walking about
option_2: It keeps the room warmer for the man
option_3: It stops the germs blowing out into the corridor
option_4: It stops the lights from shining in
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) It stops the germs blowing out into the corridor

Clinical Rationale: A shut door with airborne germs keeps them from blowing into the corridor and reaching other people.

Key Clue: why the door of a side room is kept shut

Priority Principle: Airborne isolation

Why Not Others: (a) The door is not shut to keep him in; (b) Warmth is not the reason for the shut door; (d) Light is not the reason at all.

PGI Exam Trap: The door is shut to keep the room warmer.

5-Second Recall: The shut door stops the germs leaving.

PNC Exam Pearl: Shut the door, hold the germs.

question: A 50-year-old man on the ward after a knee operation reports calf pain and a swollen leg. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Massage the calf to ease the pain
option_2: Keep the leg still and tell the doctor at once
option_3: Ask him to walk to the toilet to test it
option_4: Put a warm pack on the calf and wait
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Keep the leg still and tell the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: Calf pain with a swollen leg after surgery points to a deep vein clot, so the leg is kept still and the doctor told at once.

Key Clue: calf pain and a swollen leg after knee surgery

Priority Principle: Deep vein thrombosis

Why Not Others: (a) Massage may break off the clot; (c) Walking may move the clot to the lungs; (d) A warm pack does not treat this danger.

PGI Exam Trap: The calf is massaged to ease the pain.

5-Second Recall: Keep the leg still and tell the doctor at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: Swollen calf after surgery means a clot.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward who has an eating disorder is asked which finding needs the FIRST attention.
option_1: A very slow pulse with dizziness on standing
option_2: A steady weight over the last week
option_3: A good appetite at meal times
option_4: A calm mood during the interview
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) A very slow pulse with dizziness on standing

Clinical Rationale: A very slow pulse with dizziness points to a dangerous drop in the heart rate and needs attention FIRST.

Key Clue: a slow pulse and dizziness in an eating disorder

Priority Principle: Eating disorder risk

Why Not Others: (b) A steady weight is reassuring, not urgent; (c) A good appetite is a good sign; (d) A calm mood is not the urgent finding.

PGI Exam Trap: A calm mood during the interview is treated as urgent.

5-Second Recall: A very slow pulse with dizziness needs attention first.

PNC Exam Pearl: Slow pulse, act first.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A community nurse visits a family with a young child whose village draws drinking water from an open well. Which action is the BEST to prevent diarrhoea?
option_1: Give a vaccine against all diarrhoea
option_2: Tell the people to drink less water
option_3: Advise boiling the water and covering the well
option_4: Advise using the water without any change
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Advise boiling the water and covering the well

Clinical Rationale: Boiled or covered water stops the germs that cause diarrhoea from reaching the family.

Key Clue: water drawn from an open well

Priority Principle: Safe water

Why Not Others: (a) There is no single vaccine for all diarrhoea; (b) Drinking less water does not stop the germs; (d) Unchanged water still carries the germs.

PGI Exam Trap: The open well water is used with no change.

5-Second Recall: Advise boiling the water and covering the well.

PNC Exam Pearl: Boil it or cover it.

question: A community nurse finds that a 40-year-old man with tuberculosis lives in a small house with his family. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Tell the family to move to another house
option_2: Screen the family and start treatment if needed
option_3: Wait until the man finishes all his drugs
option_4: Give the family no advice at all
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Screen the family and start treatment if needed

Clinical Rationale: People living closely with a man who has tuberculosis are screened so that hidden cases are found and treated.

Key Clue: a man with tuberculosis living with his family

Priority Principle: Contact screening

Why Not Others: (a) The family is screened, not moved away; (c) Screening does not wait for the drugs; (d) The family is advised and helped.

PGI Exam Trap: The family is left with no advice about tuberculosis.

5-Second Recall: Screen the family and start treatment if needed.

PNC Exam Pearl: Close contacts are checked too.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward is about to do a vaginal examination. Which action is the BEST to keep her comfortable and safe?
option_1: Explain the steps and keep her covered
option_2: Start the examination without a word
option_3: Leave the door open to the corridor
option_4: Do the examination with cold hands
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Explain the steps and keep her covered

Clinical Rationale: Explaining the steps and keeping the woman covered makes the examination respectful and less stressful.

Key Clue: how to carry out a vaginal examination with care

Priority Principle: Vaginal examination

Why Not Others: (b) The woman is told what will happen first; (c) The door is closed for her privacy; (d) Cold hands make the examination painful.

PGI Exam Trap: The examination is started without telling her anything.

5-Second Recall: Explain the steps and keep her covered.

PNC Exam Pearl: Tell her, cover her, then examine.

question: A nurse on the ward must set the order of steps to insert a urinary catheter into a 60-year-old man. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST steps?
option_1: Insert the tube and explain it afterwards
option_2: Insert the tube FIRST and then clean the area
option_3: Clean the area, insert the tube, then explain
option_4: Explain, clean the area, then insert the tube
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Explain, clean the area, then insert the tube

Clinical Rationale: The nurse explains FIRST, cleans the area, and then inserts the tube so that the step is safe and understood.

Key Clue: the steps for inserting a urinary catheter

Priority Principle: Catheterisation order

Why Not Others: (a) The man is told what will happen first; (b) The area is cleaned before the tube goes in; (c) The explanation comes before the cleaning.

PGI Exam Trap: The tube is inserted before the area is cleaned.

5-Second Recall: Explain, clean, then insert.

PNC Exam Pearl: Explain, clean, insert.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has just been told of a serious illness refuses to talk about it. Which action is the BEST for the nurse to take?
option_1: Tell him that he is handling it badly
option_2: Force him to talk about the illness at once
option_3: Stay with him quietly and let him talk when ready
option_4: Leave him alone for the whole day
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Stay with him quietly and let him talk when ready

Clinical Rationale: A man who is NOT ready to talk is supported in silence and allowed to share when he feels able.

Key Clue: a man who will NOT talk about his illness

Priority Principle: Grief support

Why Not Others: (a) He is not judged for how he copes; (b) Pushing him to talk adds to his distress; (d) Leaving him alone for a day is not support.

PGI Exam Trap: The man is forced to talk about the illness at once.

5-Second Recall: Stay quietly with him and let him talk when ready.

PNC Exam Pearl: Quiet company helps grief.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who is breathing fast is asked about his blood gases. Which problem is the MOST likely for the nurse to expect?
option_1: Metabolic acidosis from diarrhoea
option_2: Respiratory acidosis from slow breathing
option_3: Metabolic alkalosis from vomiting
option_4: Respiratory alkalosis from fast breathing
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Respiratory alkalosis from fast breathing

Clinical Rationale: Fast breathing blows off carbon dioxide, so the blood turns alkaline and the picture is respiratory alkalosis.

Key Clue: fast breathing with a change in the blood gases

Priority Principle: Respiratory alkalosis

Why Not Others: (a) Diarrhoea is not the cause here; (b) Slow breathing would cause the opposite; (c) Vomiting is not the cause here.

PGI Exam Trap: Fast breathing is called a respiratory acidosis.

5-Second Recall: Fast breathing gives a respiratory alkalosis.

PNC Exam Pearl: Fast breath blows off acid.

Reference Table: Primary acid-base disorders - Metabolic acidosis: Low pH | down HCO3 | DKA, diarrhoea; Metabolic alkalosis: High pH | up HCO3 | Vomiting, diuretics; Respiratory acidosis: Low pH | up PaCO2 | COPD, sedation; Respiratory alkalosis: High pH | down PaCO2 | Hyperventilation, anxiety.

question: A nurse caring for a child on the ward is asked which finding is the MOST important sign that the child is short of breath.
option_1: Drawing in between the ribs when breathing
option_2: A calm sleep with a steady rate
option_3: A good feed with no cough
option_4: Pink lips with warm hands
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Drawing in between the ribs when breathing

Clinical Rationale: Drawing in between the ribs on breathing is a strong sign that a child is working hard to breathe.

Key Clue: a child working hard to breathe

Priority Principle: Respiratory distress

Why Not Others: (b) A calm sleep is reassuring, not a warning; (c) A good feed with no cough is a good sign; (d) Pink lips with warm hands are reassuring.

PGI Exam Trap: A calm sleep with a steady rate is called distress.

5-Second Recall: Drawing in between the ribs shows hard breathing.

PNC Exam Pearl: Ribs pulling in means hard work.

question: A community nurse visiting a family in a village finds that many children have loose stools after a flood. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take FIRST?
option_1: Move all the children to another village
option_2: Arrange safe water and treat the children FIRST
option_3: Wait for the flood water to dry up
option_4: Give the children no water at all
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Arrange safe water and treat the children FIRST

Clinical Rationale: After a flood the water is unsafe, so safe water is arranged and the children with diarrhoea are treated FIRST.

Key Clue: loose stools in children after a flood

Priority Principle: Flood and diarrhoea

Why Not Others: (a) Moving away does not fix the water; (c) Waiting lets the diarrhoea spread; (d) Stopping water makes the children drier.

PGI Exam Trap: The nurse waits for the flood water to dry up.

5-Second Recall: Arrange safe water and treat the children first.

PNC Exam Pearl: Safe water first after a flood.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked by the family to keep his serious diagnosis a secret from him. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Explain the man's right to know his own diagnosis
option_2: Agree to keep the diagnosis a secret
option_3: Tell the family to leave the ward at once
option_4: Tell the man the news without any care
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Explain the man's right to know his own diagnosis

Clinical Rationale: An alert adult has a right to know his own diagnosis, so the nurse explains this to the family with care.

Key Clue: a family asking to hide a diagnosis

Priority Principle: Right to know

Why Not Others: (b) A secret hides his right to know; (c) The family is not ordered off the ward; (d) The news is told with care, not bluntly.

PGI Exam Trap: The diagnosis is kept a secret from the man.

5-Second Recall: Explain the man's right to know his own diagnosis.

PNC Exam Pearl: The patient has a right to know.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward notes that his blood sugar is 3.0 mmol/L. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give the next insulin dose as written
option_2: Give a fast acting sugar and tell the doctor
option_3: Wait and recheck the level in four hours
option_4: Ask him to exercise to raise the level
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Give a fast acting sugar and tell the doctor

Clinical Rationale: A blood sugar of 3.0 mmol/L is too low, so fast acting sugar is given and the doctor is told at once.

Key Clue: a blood sugar of 3.0 mmol/L

Priority Principle: Hypoglycaemia

Why Not Others: (a) More insulin would lower it further; (c) Waiting risks a dangerous low; (d) Exercise lowers the sugar, not raises it.

PGI Exam Trap: The next insulin dose is given as written.

5-Second Recall: Give a fast acting sugar and tell the doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: 3.0 is low, give sugar.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward who has just given birth reports a heavy flow of blood and a soft uterus. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give a drink and let her rest
option_2: Wait and check the pad in an hour
option_3: Massage the uterus and call the doctor
option_4: Weigh the pads and do nothing else
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Massage the uterus and call the doctor

Clinical Rationale: A soft uterus with heavy bleeding points to the uterus NOT contracting, so it is massaged and the doctor called.

Key Clue: heavy bleeding with a soft uterus after birth

Priority Principle: Postpartum haemorrhage

Why Not Others: (a) A drink and rest do not stop the flow; (b) Waiting lets the bleeding continue; (d) Weighing pads alone does not stop it.

PGI Exam Trap: The pad is weighed and nothing else is done.

5-Second Recall: Massage the uterus and call the doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: Soft uterus, heavy bleed, act now.

question: A nurse on the ward must set the order of steps to give a blood transfusion to a 55-year-old man. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST steps?
option_1: Give the blood and skip the second check
option_2: Start the blood FIRST and then check the details
option_3: Check the details after the blood is running
option_4: Check the details with a second nurse, then start the blood
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Check the details with a second nurse, then start the blood

Clinical Rationale: Two nurses check the details against the man before the blood is started, so a wrong unit cannot be given.

Key Clue: the steps before starting a blood transfusion

Priority Principle: Transfusion order

Why Not Others: (a) The second check is never skipped; (b) The details are checked before the blood starts; (c) Checking after it runs is too late.

PGI Exam Trap: The blood is started before the details are checked.

5-Second Recall: Check the details with a second nurse, then start.

PNC Exam Pearl: Two nurses check first.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which blood result is the MOST likely to show poor kidney function.
option_1: A high platelet count with no bleeding
option_2: A raised blood haemoglobin with a good appetite
option_3: A low white cell count with a calm man
option_4: A raised blood creatinine with a low urine output
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) A raised blood creatinine with a low urine output

Clinical Rationale: A raised blood creatinine with a low urine output points to poor kidney function.

Key Clue: which blood result shows poor kidney function

Priority Principle: Renal function

Why Not Others: (a) Platelets are not a kidney test; (b) Haemoglobin does not show kidney function; (c) The white cell count is not a kidney test.

PGI Exam Trap: A high platelet count is used to judge kidney function.

5-Second Recall: A raised creatinine with a low urine output shows poor kidneys.

PNC Exam Pearl: Creatinine up, kidneys down.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about a deep vein clot after surgery is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: It turns into a sore on the leg over time
option_2: It stays in the leg and causes no harm
option_3: It can break off and travel to the lungs
option_4: It goes away with no treatment at all
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) It can break off and travel to the lungs

Clinical Rationale: A deep vein clot can break loose and travel to the lungs, which is why it is treated at once.

Key Clue: the danger of a deep vein clot

Priority Principle: Deep vein thrombosis risk

Why Not Others: (a) The clot does not turn into a sore; (b) A clot that travels to the lungs is dangerous; (d) A clot needs treatment and does not just go.

PGI Exam Trap: A deep vein clot stays in the leg and causes no harm.

5-Second Recall: A deep vein clot can travel to the lungs.

PNC Exam Pearl: A leg clot can reach the lung.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward notes that his hands and feet are cold while his body is warm. Which is the MOST likely cause for the nurse to consider?
option_1: A rise in the blood flow to the arms and legs
option_2: Poor blood flow to the arms and legs
option_3: A high sugar level in the blood
option_4: A low level of fluid in the body
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Poor blood flow to the arms and legs

Clinical Rationale: Cold hands and feet with a warm body point to less blood reaching the limbs, so the cause is looked for.

Key Clue: cold hands and feet with a warm body

Priority Principle: Poor limb circulation

Why Not Others: (a) More blood flow would make them warm; (c) Blood sugar is not the cause of cold limbs; (d) A low fluid level is not the direct cause.

PGI Exam Trap: The cold limbs are blamed on a high blood flow.

5-Second Recall: Cold limbs point to poor blood flow.

PNC Exam Pearl: Cold hands mean poor flow.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward tests his urine and finds sugar in it. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Report the result and check his blood sugar
option_2: Ignore the result as it means nothing
option_3: Restrict all his fluids for the day
option_4: Give him extra sugar in his drinks
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Report the result and check his blood sugar

Clinical Rationale: Sugar in the urine may point to diabetes, so the result is reported and the blood sugar is checked.

Key Clue: sugar found in the urine

Priority Principle: Sugar in urine

Why Not Others: (b) The result is reported, not set aside; (c) Restricting fluids does not treat this; (d) More sugar would worsen the problem.

PGI Exam Trap: The sugar in the urine is ignored as nothing.

5-Second Recall: Report the result and check his blood sugar.

PNC Exam Pearl: Sugar in urine, check the blood.

question: A nurse caring for a woman in the antenatal clinic notes that her blood pressure is 150/100 mmHg. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Recheck it and report it at once
option_2: Tell her that the reading is normal
option_3: Ask her to come back in a month
option_4: Give her a drug to lower it without a doctor
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Recheck it and report it at once

Clinical Rationale: A blood pressure of 150/100 mmHg in pregnancy is too high, so it is rechecked and reported at once.

Key Clue: a blood pressure of 150/100 mmHg in pregnancy

Priority Principle: High blood pressure in pregnancy

Why Not Others: (b) The reading is not normal at all; (c) Waiting a month is unsafe; (d) A drug is not given without a doctor.

PGI Exam Trap: The reading is called normal and nothing is done.

5-Second Recall: Recheck it and report it at once.

PNC Exam Pearl: 150/100 is high, report it.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about a fever is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: A fever slows the heart rate down
option_2: A fever is safe and needs no care at all
option_3: A fever lowers the body fluid need
option_4: A high fever can raise the pulse and the fluid need
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) A high fever can raise the pulse and the fluid need

Clinical Rationale: A fever raises the pulse and the need for fluid, so both are watched and fluids are offered.

Key Clue: what a fever does to the body

Priority Principle: Fever

Why Not Others: (a) A fever speeds the heart up; (b) A fever needs care, not neglect; (c) A fever raises, not lowers, the fluid need.

PGI Exam Trap: A high fever lowers the body fluid need.

5-Second Recall: A fever raises the pulse and the fluid need.

PNC Exam Pearl: Fever speed up, fluids up.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward is about to start a nasogastric feed. Which action is the BEST to check that the tube is in the stomach?
option_1: Ask the woman if it feels right
option_2: Push air down the tube and listen
option_3: Check the pH of the fluid drawn back
option_4: Start the feed and watch for a cough
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Check the pH of the fluid drawn back

Clinical Rationale: A pH of the fluid drawn back shows the tube is in the stomach and NOT in the airway.

Key Clue: how to check a nasogastric tube is in place

Priority Principle: Tube position

Why Not Others: (a) What she feels does not prove the place; (b) Air and listening alone are not reliable; (d) A cough after the feed is too late.

PGI Exam Trap: The tube is checked by pushing air and listening only.

5-Second Recall: Check the pH of the fluid drawn back.

PNC Exam Pearl: Check the pH to know the place.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward with a large burn is asked which finding is the MOST important to show that he needs more fluid.
option_1: A steady urine output with a calm pulse
option_2: A falling urine output with a rising pulse
option_3: A dry dressing with no ooze
option_4: A good appetite at meal times
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) A falling urine output with a rising pulse

Clinical Rationale: A falling urine output with a rising pulse shows the body is short of fluid after a large burn.

Key Clue: a large burn with a rising pulse

Priority Principle: Fluid loss after a burn

Why Not Others: (a) A steady output with a calm pulse is reassuring; (c) A dry dressing does not show fluid loss; (d) A good appetite does not show a fluid need.

PGI Exam Trap: A steady urine output with a calm pulse shows the need for more fluid.

5-Second Recall: A falling urine output with a rising pulse shows a fluid need.

PNC Exam Pearl: Less urine, faster pulse, more fluid.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about a leg ulcer from poor veins is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: It needs no dressing at all
option_2: It is treated by cutting off the leg
option_3: It is treated with a firm bandage and leg raising
option_4: It heals BEST when the leg hangs down
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) It is treated with a firm bandage and leg raising

Clinical Rationale: A venous ulcer heals with a firm bandage and the leg raised, which helps the blood flow back up.

Key Clue: how a leg ulcer from poor veins is treated

Priority Principle: Venous leg ulcer

Why Not Others: (a) The ulcer needs a dressing and care; (b) Cutting off the leg is not the treatment; (d) The leg is raised, not left hanging.

PGI Exam Trap: The leg is left hanging down to help the ulcer.

5-Second Recall: A firm bandage and leg raising treat it.

PNC Exam Pearl: Bandage and raise the leg.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about pressure sores is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: They heal faster with more pressure on them
option_2: They form on the front of the body in MOST people
option_3: They are caused by too much movement
option_4: They form over bony points in a person who cannot move
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) They form over bony points in a person who cannot move

Clinical Rationale: Pressure sores form over bony points when a person cannot move, because the skin is pressed and the blood flow is cut.

Key Clue: how pressure sores form

Priority Principle: Pressure sore

Why Not Others: (a) More pressure makes them worse; (b) They form over bony points, not the front; (c) Too little movement, not too much, causes them.

PGI Exam Trap: Pressure sores are caused by too much movement.

5-Second Recall: They form over bony points in a person who cannot move.

PNC Exam Pearl: Still and bony, skin breaks.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward is asked which statement about the FIRST stage of labour is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The cervix opens fully during this stage
option_2: The baby is born during this stage
option_3: The placenta comes out during this stage
option_4: The uterus stops working during this stage
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The cervix opens fully during this stage

Clinical Rationale: The FIRST stage of labour lasts until the cervix is fully open, ready for the baby to be born.

Key Clue: what happens in the FIRST stage of labour

Priority Principle: First stage of labour

Why Not Others: (b) The baby is born in the second stage; (c) The placenta comes out in the third stage; (d) The uterus works hard in this stage.

PGI Exam Trap: The baby is born during the FIRST stage.

5-Second Recall: The cervix opens fully in the first stage.

PNC Exam Pearl: First stage opens the neck of the womb.

question: A nurse on the ward must set the order of steps to draw up insulin for a man with diabetes. In which order should the nurse take the FIRST steps?
option_1: Draw the dose FIRST and then check the order
option_2: Check the order, clean the top, then draw the dose
option_3: Clean the top, draw the dose, then check the order
option_4: Draw the dose and check the order afterwards
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Check the order, clean the top, then draw the dose

Clinical Rationale: The order is checked, the top of the vial is cleaned, and then the dose is drawn up safely.

Key Clue: the steps for drawing up insulin

Priority Principle: Insulin order

Why Not Others: (a) The order is checked before the dose; (c) Checking the order comes before cleaning; (d) The order is checked first, not after.

PGI Exam Trap: The dose is drawn before the order is checked.

5-Second Recall: Check the order, clean the top, then draw.

PNC Exam Pearl: Check, clean, draw.

question: A nurse caring for a child on the ward is asked which statement about a child's fluid need is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: A child's fluid need does NOT change with fever
option_2: A small child needs less water than an adult
option_3: A small child needs more water for each kilogram than an adult
option_4: A child needs no extra fluid when hot
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) A small child needs more water for each kilogram than an adult

Clinical Rationale: A small child has more body water for each kilogram, so the fluid need for each kilogram is higher than in an adult.

Key Clue: how much water a small child needs

Priority Principle: Child fluid need

Why Not Others: (a) Fever raises a child's fluid need; (b) A child needs more, not less, for each kilogram; (d) Heat raises the fluid need, not lowers it.

PGI Exam Trap: A small child needs less water than an adult.

5-Second Recall: A child needs more water for each kilogram.

PNC Exam Pearl: Small body, more water for its size.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A community nurse caring for a family is asked which statement about the infant death rate is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: It counts deaths of all children under five years
option_2: It counts deaths of babies under one year for each 1000 births
option_3: It counts deaths of mothers during childbirth
option_4: It counts all deaths in the village in a year
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) It counts deaths of babies under one year for each 1000 births

Clinical Rationale: The infant death rate counts deaths of babies under one year of age for every 1000 live births.

Key Clue: what the infant death rate counts

Priority Principle: Infant death rate

Why Not Others: (a) That is the under-five rate, not the infant rate; (c) Death of mothers is the maternal rate; (d) All deaths in a village is a crude rate.

PGI Exam Trap: The infant death rate counts all deaths in the village.

5-Second Recall: It counts deaths of babies under one year.

PNC Exam Pearl: Under one year, per 1000 births.

question: A nurse caring for a woman in the antenatal clinic reports that her waters have broken but she has no pain and the head is high. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Admit her at once and check the baby's heart
option_2: Send her home to come back in two days
option_3: Ask her to wait for pain before coming in
option_4: Give a drug to start the pain at home
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Admit her at once and check the baby's heart

Clinical Rationale: Waters breaking with a high head risks a cord prolapse, so the woman is admitted at once and the baby checked.

Key Clue: waters broken with a high head and no pain

Priority Principle: Rupture of membranes

Why Not Others: (b) Sending her home risks the cord; (c) Waiting for pain is unsafe here; (d) Labour is not started at home like this.

PGI Exam Trap: The woman is sent home to wait two days.

5-Second Recall: Admit her at once and check the baby's heart.

PNC Exam Pearl: Waters out, high head, admit now.

question: A nurse manager on the ward is asked which action BEST helps a new nurse settle into the team over 6 weeks.
option_1: Tell him NOT to ask any questions
option_2: Give him the hardest patients alone on day one
option_3: Leave him to work it out on his own
option_4: Pair him with a senior nurse for the FIRST weeks
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Pair him with a senior nurse for the FIRST weeks

Clinical Rationale: Pairing a new nurse with a senior for the FIRST weeks gives support while his skills and confidence grow.

Key Clue: how to help a new nurse settle in

Priority Principle: Preceptorship

Why Not Others: (a) Questions are welcome, not barred; (b) The hardest patients alone on day one is unsafe; (c) Working it out alone gives no support.

PGI Exam Trap: The new nurse is left alone with the hardest patients.

5-Second Recall: Pair him with a senior nurse for the first weeks.

PNC Exam Pearl: Give a new nurse a helper at first.

question: A nurse manager on the ward is asked which action is the BEST to prevent a drug error on the unit.
option_1: Let any staff member give any drug
option_2: Ask the nurses to work faster to save time
option_3: Keep the drug cupboard unlocked
option_4: Use a clear double check for high-alert drugs
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Use a clear double check for high-alert drugs

Clinical Rationale: A clear double check by two nurses for high-alert drugs catches mistakes before the drug reaches the man.

Key Clue: how to prevent a drug error on the unit

Priority Principle: Double check

Why Not Others: (a) Not every staff member gives every drug; (b) Working faster raises the chance of error; (c) An unlocked cupboard invites mistakes.

PGI Exam Trap: The drug cupboard is left unlocked to save time.

5-Second Recall: Use a clear double check for high-alert drugs.

PNC Exam Pearl: Two checks stop one error.

question: A community nurse visiting a family finds a man with a deep cough and weight loss for two months. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take FIRST?
option_1: Send a sputum sample to the lab for testing
option_2: Give him a cough syrup and send him home
option_3: Tell him that the weather is the cause
option_4: Wait and see if he improves in a month
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Send a sputum sample to the lab for testing

Clinical Rationale: A deep cough with weight loss for two months may be tuberculosis, so a sputum sample is sent to the lab.

Key Clue: a deep cough and weight loss for two months

Priority Principle: Possible tuberculosis

Why Not Others: (b) A cough syrup does not find the cause; (c) The weather is not the cause here; (d) Waiting lets the illness spread.

PGI Exam Trap: The man is sent home with only a cough syrup.

5-Second Recall: Send a sputum sample to the lab for testing.

PNC Exam Pearl: Long cough with weight loss, test the sputum.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who takes vancomycin is asked which finding is the MOST important to show that his drug level is too high.
option_1: A trough level below the safe range
option_2: A trough level above the safe range
option_3: A normal blood count with no change
option_4: A good urine output with no pain
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) A trough level above the safe range

Clinical Rationale: A trough level above the safe range means too much vancomycin, which can harm the ears and kidneys.

Key Clue: a vancomycin trough level above the safe range

Priority Principle: Drug levels

Why Not Others: (a) A level below the range is too low; (c) The blood count is not the drug level; (d) A good urine output does not show the level.

Clinical Rationale: Extra oxygen before suctioning and a short suction time stop the oxygen level from falling.

Key Clue: how to suction a tracheostomy safely

Priority Principle: Suctioning

Why Not Others: (a) The tube is not left in the airway; (b) A long suction drops the oxygen level; (c) Oxygen is given before the suction.

PGI Exam Trap: A long suction is done to clear the airway fully.

5-Second Recall: Give extra oxygen before and keep the suction short.

PNC Exam Pearl: Oxygen first, suction brief.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village is asked which statement about herd immunity is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: Many immunised people protect those who cannot be immunised
option_2: One immunised person protects the whole village
option_3: Immunity works for the person who is immunised and no one else
option_4: A vaccine gives no protection to anybody at all
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Many immunised people protect those who cannot be immunised

Clinical Rationale: When many people are immunised, the germs cannot spread easily and the few who cannot be immunised are protected.

Key Clue: how herd immunity protects a village

Priority Principle: Herd immunity

Why Not Others: (b) One person cannot protect the whole village; (c) Immunity spreads protection to others; (d) A vaccine does protect people from disease.

PGI Exam Trap: One immunised person is said to protect the whole village.

5-Second Recall: Many immunised people protect those who cannot be.

PNC Exam Pearl: Many protected, all protected.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about the blood test that shows clotting ability is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The haemoglobin shows the clotting ability
option_2: The platelet count shows the clotting ability
option_3: The blood sugar shows the clotting ability
option_4: The creatinine shows the clotting ability
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The platelet count shows the clotting ability

Clinical Rationale: The platelet count shows how well the blood can clot, so a low count raises the risk of bleeding.

Key Clue: which blood test shows clotting ability

Priority Principle: Platelet count

Why Not Others: (a) Haemoglobin carries oxygen, not clotting; (c) Blood sugar is not about clotting; (d) Creatinine shows kidney function.

PGI Exam Trap: The haemoglobin is said to show the clotting ability.

5-Second Recall: The platelet count shows the clotting ability.

PNC Exam Pearl: Platelets make the plug.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has been in bed for a week is asked which problem he is MOST likely to face.
option_1: A runny nose from the ward air
option_2: A high blood sugar from NOT eating
option_3: A blood clot in the leg from NOT moving
option_4: A toothache from the hospital food
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) A blood clot in the leg from NOT moving

Clinical Rationale: Staying in bed for a week slows the blood flow, so a clot in the leg is the main risk.

Key Clue: a man in bed for a week

Priority Principle: Immobility risk

Why Not Others: (a) A runny nose is not the main risk; (b) Not eating lowers, not raises, the sugar; (d) A toothache is not caused by the food here.

PGI Exam Trap: A runny nose from the ward air is the main risk.

5-Second Recall: A blood clot in the leg is the main risk.

PNC Exam Pearl: Still legs breed clots.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about the spread of infection by droplets is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: Droplets pass into the body through the skin
option_2: Droplets travel many metres through the air
option_3: Droplets stay in the air for several days
option_4: Droplets travel a short way when a person coughs
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Droplets travel a short way when a person coughs

Clinical Rationale: Droplets from a cough travel only a short way before they fall, so close contact spreads them.

Key Clue: how droplets spread infection

Priority Principle: Droplet spread

Why Not Others: (a) Droplets enter by the nose or mouth; (b) Droplets do not travel many metres; (c) Droplets do not stay in the air for days.

PGI Exam Trap: Droplets are said to travel many metres.

5-Second Recall: Droplets travel a short way from a cough.

PNC Exam Pearl: Droplets fall close by.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about a drain after surgery is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The drain does NOT need any recording
option_2: The drain is left in until it stops hurting
option_3: The drain is pulled out by the nurse at once
option_4: The amount and colour of the fluid are recorded
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The amount and colour of the fluid are recorded

Clinical Rationale: The amount and colour of the fluid from a drain are recorded so a bleed or infection is spotted early.

Key Clue: what is recorded about a surgical drain

Priority Principle: Surgical drain

Why Not Others: (a) The fluid amount and colour are recorded; (b) The drain is kept in for its own reason; (c) The nurse does not pull it out at once.

PGI Exam Trap: The drain is pulled out by the nurse at once.

5-Second Recall: The amount and colour of the fluid are recorded.

PNC Exam Pearl: Watch what the drain gives.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which food is the MOST appropriate source of iron.
option_1: Dark green leafy vegetables and liver
option_2: White bread with butter and jam
option_3: Milk and cheese with a little sugar
option_4: Plain boiled rice with sugar on top
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Dark green leafy vegetables and liver

Clinical Rationale: Dark green leafy vegetables and liver hold a lot of iron, which the body uses to make red blood cells.

Key Clue: which food is a good source of iron

Priority Principle: Iron sources

Why Not Others: (b) White bread with jam has little iron; (c) Milk and cheese have little iron; (d) Rice with sugar has little iron.

PGI Exam Trap: White bread with jam is called a good iron source.

5-Second Recall: Green leafy vegetables and liver are rich in iron.

PNC Exam Pearl: Greens and liver give iron.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about paracetamol overdose is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The antidote works BEST after the liver fails
option_2: The antidote is given early and the liver is watched
option_3: No treatment is needed if he feels well
option_4: The damage shows at once in the man
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The antidote is given early and the liver is watched

Clinical Rationale: In paracetamol overdose the antidote is given early to protect the liver, and the liver is watched closely.

Key Clue: what to do in a paracetamol overdose

Priority Principle: Paracetamol overdose

Why Not Others: (a) The antidote is given before the liver fails; (c) Feeling well does not mean no damage; (d) The damage may show only after days.

PGI Exam Trap: Feeling well means no treatment is needed.

5-Second Recall: Give the antidote early and watch the liver.

PNC Exam Pearl: Antidote early, liver watched.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has a head injury is asked which finding is the MOST important to show rising pressure inside the head.
option_1: A good appetite with no headache
option_2: A rising level of consciousness with a fast pulse
option_3: A falling level of consciousness with a slow pulse
option_4: A calm sleep with a normal pulse
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) A falling level of consciousness with a slow pulse

Clinical Rationale: A falling level of consciousness with a slow pulse is a classic sign of rising pressure inside the head.

Key Clue: a falling level of consciousness with a slow pulse

Priority Principle: Rising head pressure

Why Not Others: (a) A good appetite with no headache is not this; (b) A rising level of consciousness is reassuring; (d) A calm sleep with a normal pulse is not this.

PGI Exam Trap: A rising level of consciousness shows rising head pressure.

5-Second Recall: A falling level of consciousness with a slow pulse.

PNC Exam Pearl: Drowsier and slow pulse means rising pressure.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward is asked which action is the BEST to prevent a pressure sore.
option_1: Turn her every two hours and check the skin
option_2: Leave her in one position all day
option_3: Rub the red areas firmly each day
option_4: Keep the sheets creased under her
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Turn her every two hours and check the skin

Clinical Rationale: Turning the woman every two hours and checking the skin reduces the pressure on bony points and stops sores forming.

Key Clue: how to prevent a pressure sore

Priority Principle: Pressure sore prevention

Why Not Others: (b) One position all day presses the skin; (c) Rubbing red areas can damage the skin; (d) Creased sheets press and rub the skin.

PGI Exam Trap: The woman is left in one position all day.

5-Second Recall: Turn her every two hours and check the skin.

PNC Exam Pearl: Turn often, check the skin.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about oxygen therapy is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The flow rate is set to the highest possible
option_2: The flow rate is set on the doctor's order
option_3: Oxygen is safe at any flow rate chosen
option_4: The oxygen is turned off for a walk outside
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The flow rate is set on the doctor's order

Clinical Rationale: The oxygen flow rate is set to the doctor's order because too much or too little can both harm the man.

Key Clue: how the oxygen flow rate is set

Priority Principle: Oxygen therapy

Why Not Others: (a) The highest rate is not set at random; (c) Too much oxygen can harm a man; (d) The oxygen is not simply turned off.

PGI Exam Trap: The flow rate is set to the highest possible.

5-Second Recall: The flow rate is set on the doctor's order.

PNC Exam Pearl: Set the rate as ordered.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who has been on bed rest for a long time is asked to help him stand for the FIRST time. Which action is the BEST?
option_1: Let him walk to the bathroom alone
option_2: Stand him up quickly to save time
option_3: Raise him slowly and stay close beside him
option_4: Leave him sitting with no support
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Raise him slowly and stay close beside him

Clinical Rationale: Raising a man slowly and staying close reduces the dizziness that comes after a long time in bed.

Key Clue: helping a man stand after a long bed rest

Priority Principle: First stand after bed rest

Why Not Others: (a) Walking alone risks a fall; (b) Standing him up quickly causes dizziness; (d) No support puts him at risk of a fall.

PGI Exam Trap: The man is stood up quickly to save time.

5-Second Recall: Raise him slowly and stay close beside him.

PNC Exam Pearl: Up slowly, stay close.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about writing the nursing record is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The record is left blank when busy
option_2: The record is written from memory next week
option_3: Mistakes are covered over with black ink
option_4: The record is written at the time of the care
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The record is written at the time of the care

Clinical Rationale: The nursing record is written at the time of the care so that it is a true and clear account.

Key Clue: when a nursing record is written

Priority Principle: Record keeping

Why Not Others: (a) The record is not left blank when busy; (b) Writing from memory next week is not accurate; (c) Mistakes are crossed out clearly and signed.

PGI Exam Trap: The record is written from memory the next week.

5-Second Recall: The record is written at the time of the care.

PNC Exam Pearl: Write it when you do it.
